channel.title: Cortrix Blog
channel.description: Practical readings of foundational papers on semantic systems and agent memory.

item.title: DBpedia explained: why linked data still matters
item.description: A practical reading of the 2007 DBpedia paper: RDF, stable entity identity, linked data, and what they mean for semantic storage and AI agents.
item.dc:creator: Scott

item.title: TransE explained: relationships beyond vector similarity
item.description: How TransE uses h + r ≈ t to learn knowledge graph embeddings, where its simple model breaks down, and why vectors still need explicit relationships.
item.dc:creator: Scott

item.title: RAG explained: external memory brings data governance back
item.description: Read the original RAG paper through a database engineer's lens: parametric memory, retrieval, RAG-Sequence, RAG-Token, and the limits of grounding.
item.dc:creator: Scott

item.title: Reflexion explained: agent memory without weight updates
item.description: How Reflexion turns feedback into agent memory, why the evaluator matters, and what its experiments do and do not establish about learning from failure.
item.dc:creator: Scott

item.title: HippoRAG explained: why RAG comes back to knowledge graphs
item.description: How the original HippoRAG combines knowledge graphs and Personalized PageRank for retrieval across documents, with a close look at its limits.
item.dc:creator: Scott
